collection_summary: This instance is an exhaustive historical slice over a single source-defined accession list. It uses the explicit country-year list of eurozone entrants on the Wikipedia page 'Enlargement of the eurozone' and keeps only entrants from 1999 through 2023.
source_coverage_notes: The cited page explicitly states that the first 11 eurozone members introduced the euro on 1 January 1999, then names Greece (2001), Slovenia (2007), Cyprus and Malta (2008), Slovakia (2009), Estonia (2011), Latvia (2014), Lithuania (2015), Croatia (2023), and Bulgaria (2026). This instance keeps all countries in that explicit historical list through 2023 and excludes only Bulgaria because it falls outside the query range.
decision_log: Chose a single-source temporal instance as a forward test of the curation skill because it is easier to verify than a multi-source fuzzy-join case while still adding a new benchmark category not present in cfg.json. The initial 2001-2023 draft had only 9 rows and failed the protocol minimum-row criterion, so the query was widened to 1999-2023. Marked the claim type as exhaustive because the source text itself is an explicit historical accession list rather than a 'major examples' subset.
normalization_decisions: Country names follow the source page's English article names. Adoption years are stored as bare integers. The table uses Country as the primary key because each country appears once in the filtered historical slice.
open_questions: If later benchmark policy prefers only sources more authoritative than Wikipedia for treaty-history questions, this instance could be rebuilt from EU or ECB historical accession materials. Otherwise the current source is sufficient for a stable, easily auditable temporal benchmark item.
